questions.text: What does the resistance of a conductor depend on?
answers: on the material of the conductor and its geometric dimensions.
on the current in the conductor and the voltage.

questions.text: If the voltage across the ends of a conductor is increased, its resistance...
Which of the given formulas expresses the dependence of a conductor's resistance on its length?

A tungsten wire $40$ cm long with a cross-sectional area of $0,002$ mm$^2$ is taken to make the filament of an incandescent lamp. The resistivity of tungsten is $5.5\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m. Find the resistance of the filament ($\Omega$).
Find the resistance of a copper wire $50$ m long with a cross-sectional area of $34$ mm$^2$ (m$\Omega$). The resistivity of copper is $1.7\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
The resistance of a nickelin wire $210$ m long is $14.7~\Omega$. Find its cross-sectional area (mm$^2$). $\rho=4.2\cdot10^{-7}~\Omega\cdot$m.
The cross-sectional area of an aluminum wire is $0.5$ cm$^2$ and its resistance is $2.8~\Omega$. Find the length of the wire (m). $\rho=2.8\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
How many meters long must a copper wire with a cross-sectional area of $0.17$ mm$^2$ be for its resistance to be $9~\Omega$? The resistivity of copper is $1.7\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
For a voltage of $12$ mV, determine the current (mA) in a steel wire $10$ m long with a cross-section of $2$ mm$^2$. $\rho=12\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.

A DC power transmission line is made of wire with a cross-sectional area of $150$ mm$^2$, a resistivity of $2.8\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m and a length of $150$ km. What is the voltage drop along the line (in volts) if the current is $100$ A?

In an aluminum wire $500$ km long with a cross-sectional area of $10$ mm$^2$, a current of $10$ mA flows. What is the voltage across its ends (in volts)? The resistivity of aluminum is $2.8\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.

A rheostat made of nickelin wire with a cross-section of $1$ mm$^2$ is connected to an ammeter reading $20$ A and a voltmeter reading $210$ V ($\rho=4.2\cdot10^{-7}~\Omega\cdot$m). How many meters long is the rheostat wire?
How does the resistance of a conductor change if its cross-sectional area is increased $2$ times and its length $3$ times?
The resistance of a copper wire is $6~\Omega$. What is the resistance of a copper wire whose cross-sectional area is $3$ times larger and whose length is $2$ times larger ($\Omega$)?
The electrical resistance of a copper wire is $6~\Omega$. What is the resistance of a copper wire whose length is $3$ times larger and whose diameter is $2$ times larger ($\Omega$)?
The electrical resistance of a copper wire is $6~\Omega$. What is the resistance of a copper wire whose length is $3$ times larger and whose diameter is $2$ times smaller ($\Omega$)?

A conductor of length $l$ and cross-sectional area $S$ has an electrical resistance of $4~\Omega$. What resistance will a conductor made of the same material, of length $2l$ and cross-sectional area $S/4$, have?

The first conductor has a length of $1$ m and a cross-sectional area of $1$ mm$^2$; the second has a length of $2$ m and a cross-sectional area of $0.5$ mm$^2$. How are the resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ of these conductors related?

Of two aluminum wires of equal length, one has a resistance of $2.7~\Omega$ and the other $1.8~\Omega$. The cross-sectional area of the first wire is $4$ mm$^2$. What is the cross-sectional area of the second wire (mm$^2$)?
For two conductors of equal length with cross-sectional areas $S_1=2S_2$ and resistivities $\rho_2=2\rho_1$, determine the ratio of their resistances $R_2/R_1$.

The resistance of a conductor $1$ m long with a cross-sectional area of $0.5$ mm$^2$ equals the resistance of a wire of the same material with a cross-sectional area of $10$ mm$^2$. How many meters of such wire must be taken?

Find the resistance of a silver wire with a cross-sectional area of $1$ mm$^2$ and a weight of $105$ N ($\Omega$). The density of silver is $10500$ kg/m$^3$ and its resistivity is $1.6\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
One wire is $20$ cm long and another is $1.6$ m long. The wires have the same cross-section and are made of the same material. Which wire has the greater resistance, and by what factor?
answers: the first, by a factor of 3.2.
the second, by a factor of 3.2.
the first, by a factor of 8.
the second, by a factor of 8.

questions.text: How does the resistance of a metal wire change if its length and radius are increased $4$ times?
By what factor does the resistance of a wire increase if it is stretched so that its length becomes $3$ times greater?
How does the resistance of a resistor change if the source voltage is increased $2$ times?
How does the resistance of a resistor change if the current in the circuit is increased $5$ times?
Two wires are made from equal masses of metal. One of them is $3$ times longer than the other. Determine the relation between the resistances $R_1$ and $R_2$ of these wires.

What is the resistance of a copper wire of mass $8.9$ kg with a cross-sectional area of $1$ mm$^2$ ($\Omega$)? The density of copper is $8.9$ g/cm$^3$ and its resistivity is $1.7\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.

Determine the resistance of a steel rail whose mass per meter is $3.9$ kg and whose length is $1$ km ($\Omega$). The density of steel is $7800$ kg/m$^3$ and its resistivity is $1.2\cdot10^{-7}~\Omega\cdot$m.
A steel rail with a mass of $1$ m equal to $78$ kg has a resistance of $0,012~\Omega$ per meter? The density of steel is $7.8$ g/cm$^3$ and its resistivity is $1.2\cdot10^{-7}~\Omega\cdot$m.
What is the mass of a conductor of length $l$, resistance $R$, density $d$ and resistivity $\rho$?
The resistance of a copper wire $1$ km long is $75.65~\Omega$. How many newtons does the wire weigh? The density of copper is $8900$ kg/m$^3$ and its resistivity is $1.7\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
A current of $6$ A flows through an electric coil. What current (in amperes) will flow through it if a quarter of the coil is cut off? $U=\text{const}$.
How does the resistance of a wire change if it is cut into two equal pieces and both pieces are laid side by side (in parallel)?
A long conductor was cut into two equal pieces and twisted together along its length into a single conductor. How does the resistance of the conductor change?
A wire of resistance $R$ was cut into three equal pieces and all three pieces were twisted together along their length. What will the resistance of the wire be?
A conductor was cut into 5 pieces and twisted tightly together; its resistance became $1~\Omega$. Find the initial resistance of the conductor ($\Omega$).
A wire of resistance $R$ was cut into four equal pieces and all four pieces were twisted together along their length. What will the resistance of such a wire be?
How does the resistance of a conductor (without insulation) change if it is folded in two and twisted?
What is the electric field strength inside a metal wire if its resistivity is $\rho$, its cross-sectional area is $S$ and the current in it is $I$?

What is the electric field strength (V/m) inside a copper wire through which a steady current of $20$ A flows, if its cross-sectional area is $1$ mm$^2$? The resistivity of copper is $1.7\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
What is the field strength inside an aluminum conductor (V/m) if the current density in it is $2\cdot10^6$ A/m$^2$? The resistivity of aluminum is $2\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
To a conductor $10$ m long with a resistivity of $5\cdot10^{-7}~\Omega\cdot$m a voltage of $10$ V is applied. What is the current density in the conductor (A/m$^2$)?
The voltage drop across a nichrome wire $2$ m long is $2.5$ V. What is the current density in it (A/m$^2$)? The resistivity of nichrome is $1\cdot10^{-6}~\Omega\cdot$m.
The current density in a copper wire is $1$ A/mm$^2$. What is the electric field strength in the wire (V/m)? The resistivity of copper is $1.7\cdot10^{-8}~\Omega\cdot$m.
The same voltage is applied to two conductors made of the same material, with length ratio $l_2/l_1=2$ and cross-sectional area ratio $S_2/S_1=2$. How are the current densities in them related?
How does the current density in a conductor change if, without changing its length or the potential difference applied to it, its cross-sectional area is reduced $2$ times?
How does the current in a metal wire change if the electric field strength in it decreases $8$ times and the cross-sectional area of the wire increases $10$ times?
